title: Fair Share Paper Pizza
subject: math
learningGoal: Understand halves and quarters as equal parts of a whole.
realWorldHook: When we share food, everyone wants a fair piece. Fair means equal.

materials.householdSubstitution: Any paper; a square works too

noPurchaseRoute: Trace a plate on any paper and cut it out, or just fold a square sheet.
parentPreview: Your child folds a paper 'pizza' to share fairly between 2, then 4 people, and checks the pieces are equal by laying them on top of each other.

parent.parentSays: If two of us share a pizza, how can we make it fair?

child.screen: How can 2 people share a pizza fairly?
child.readAloudText: How can two people share a pizza fairly?

parent.parentSays: Fold the circle so both sides match exactly. Open it. How many pieces? Are they the same size?
parent.whyThisWorks: Matching edges is a physical way to check 'equal'.

child.screen: Fold the pizza so both sides match. How many pieces?
child.readAloudText: Fold so both sides match. How many pieces?

parent.parentSays: Now fold it again to share with four people. How many pieces now?
parent.whyThisWorks: Seeing that more people means smaller pieces builds intuition for fractions.

child.screen: Fold again for 4 people. How many pieces now?
child.readAloudText: Fold again for four people. How many pieces?

parent.parentSays: Ask which piece is bigger, a quarter or a half, then ask how they know.

child.screen: Is one quarter bigger or smaller than one half?
child.readAloudText: Is one quarter bigger or smaller than one half?

parent.parentSays: Ask the two check questions below. Give your child time to think, then note how each one went.
Where else do we share things fairly at home?

expectedResponses: A quarter is smaller than a half

misconceptions.signal: Calls any two pieces 'halves' even when one is clearly bigger.
misconceptions.supportiveNextQuestion: Let's lay the pieces on top of each other. Do they match exactly?

misconceptions.signal: Thinks a quarter is bigger than a half because 4 is bigger than 2.
misconceptions.supportiveNextQuestion: If four people share, does each person get more or less than if two share?

checkQuestions.parentAsks: If we cut a pizza into 2 pieces that don't match, is it halves?

interpretation.clear: Says no, halves must be equal.
interpretation.not_yet: Says yes, any 2 pieces are halves.

child.screen: 2 pieces that don't match. Are they halves?
child.readAloudText: Two pieces that don't match. Are they halves?

checkQuestions.parentAsks: Would you rather have half a sandwich or a quarter of the same sandwich? Why?

interpretation.clear: Chooses half and explains it's bigger.

child.screen: Half a sandwich or a quarter of a sandwich: which is more?
child.readAloudText: Half a sandwich or a quarter of a sandwich. Which is more?

extension: Fold into eighths. Can you make a fair share for 3 people? (Harder!)

shorterVersion.description: Halves and quarters only, then the check.

accessibilityAdaptations: Pre-draw fold lines for easier folding.
Use a real sandwich or toast instead of paper.
